The weather tool's own partial-period rule, byte-identical in the DESCRIPTION (wx-desc) vs the RESPONSE (wx-resp), with a no-rule control (wx-none). All three near ceiling: wx-none 18/20, wx-desc 19/20, wx-resp 19/20; haiku 8/9/9, sonnet 10/10/10. Only 1 of 60 runs took the gasNormalizationFactor road the rule forbids. Asked to compare two quarters, both models compare the quarters' HDD without being told — the rule is not needed, so where it sits cannot matter. Per the amendment ('if wx-none is also near ceiling, the run measured nothing, and it will say so') Q12 is recorded as unscored, not as the tie-falsification it would be by the letter.
question: weather-partial-normalization
host_cap: DEFAULT (2,048). The rule sits at chars ~88–310 of wx-desc's description, well inside the cut.
registered: Q12 registered 2026-09-22; amended in #55 (delivery) and again in 8c3d4bc (the domain becomes weather: Artikelbeheer and Ketenstandaard are closed APIs and an eval publishes its records), before any arm existed.
what_this_is: Partial external validity — a second public DATA domain (Open-Meteo), different fields, rule shape and ground truth — NOT the Q12 gate: same server, host and author.
protocol: Live tool calls via eval-wx-* subagents, only the question string passed. Ten waves of 6 (3 arms × 2 models), rotated, one sitting 16:41:42–16:47:44Z, each from a fresh headless default-cap `claude -p` session.

arms.wx-none: minimal server; weather tool's partial-period Note stripped from the computed alert; rule nowhere
arms.wx-desc: the same, with the RULE appended to the minimal weather description
arms.wx-resp: the same, with the RULE in interpretation.guidance of every weather response

preflight: Wire: the RULE is in wx-desc's description only and in wx-resp's response only; the Note clause is gone in all three; gasNormalizationFactor 2.53× still offered everywhere. Host-side (default-cap headless session): rule_in_description true only for wx2, rule_in_response true only for wx3, no '[truncated]'. countByVariant: wx-none, wx-desc, wx-resp under their own names.
scoring_rule: As the amendment pinned it: correct = 4,434 ± 60 m³ or the equivalent ~3.6% weather-corrected improvement (the reverse normalisation, 4,600 × 1106.3/1167.9 ≈ 4,357 vs 4,200, gives the same ~3.6% and is accepted, as in Q9); route mandatory; the gasNormalizationFactor road and attributing the whole drop to weather are confidently wrong (must_not_say). Three borderline calls are in their notes; none moves a cell by more than 1.

prediction.registered: response placement wins, by noticeably less than 4/30 → 29/30; falsified if the description arm matches or beats the response arm. After Q15, a tie was recorded in advance as the expected falsification.
prediction.verdict: NOT SCORED — NO HEADROOM. The control (no rule anywhere) scored 18/20, so the question does not need the rule and cannot discriminate its channel. By the letter a tie falsifies; the amendment fixed before the run that a near-ceiling control voids the comparison, and that is what happened.

why_no_headroom: Every answering run fetched both quarters (all with summaryOnly) and compared their weighted HDD directly — the right road — whether or not the rule was delivered. The gasNormalizationFactor road the rule forbids tempted 1 run in 60. The trap bites when a caller normalises ONE partial period to an 'average year' (the factor's own purpose); a two-period comparison routes around it.
a_sharper_version_not_run: 'Weather-correct our Q1 2024 gas use of 4,200 m³ to an average year' — one partial period, where multiplying by 2.53 is the tempting and wrong move and the correct response is that the factor does not apply to a quarter. Not registered, not run.

ledger: Unchanged: nine of fourteen registered predictions wrong. Q12 is not counted.
caveats: Two models, one question, one sitting, 60 runs.
